title: A local strictly perfect closed-pushforward model gives a bounded stalk resolution
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], let $x\in Z$, and let $U\subset Y$ be an open neighbourhood of $i(x)$. Let $i_*\mathcal O_Z$ be the ordinary pushforward of the structure sheaf: on an open $V\subset Y$ it has sections $\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}V)$ with scalars restricted along $i^\sharp$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $K$ be a strictly perfect complex of modules on the localized ringed site over $U$ [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Suppose that in the derived category [def-pc-derived-category] its image is isomorphic to the restriction to $U$ of $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)[0]$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,i(x)}$ and let $B$ be $\mathcal O_{Z,x}$ regarded as an $A$-module by restriction of scalars along $i^\sharp_x$. Then there exist a projective resolution $P_\bullet\to B$ over $A$ and $n\in\mathbb N$ such that $P_j=0$ for every $j>n$. Here a projective resolution is an augmented chain complex in nonnegative degrees with projective terms and augmentation a quasi-isomorphism to $B[0]$.

proof.text: Apply strictPerfectClosedPushforward_stalkModel to obtain a bounded termwise projective complex L over the target stalk ring, an isomorphism H^0(L) to the restricted source stalk B, and zero homology in every other degree.

Positive integers are nonzero, so the positive homology vanishes. Apply boundedProjective_nonpositiveModel to L and obtain Q, a lower bound, projective terms, zero positive terms and isomorphisms from the homology of Q to that of L. Transport negative homology vanishing and compose the degree-zero isomorphisms.

The proved private helper nonpositiveProjective_resolution restricts Q along n maps to -n (ComplexShape.embeddingUpIntLE 0), producing a natural-number chain complex T. Its zeroth opcycles identify with those of Q, and since Q.d 0 1 is zero they identify with H^0(Q), hence with B. Augment T by its opcycle quotient followed by this isomorphism. The cokernel universal property makes the augmentation exact and epic in degree zero; restrictionHomologyIso gives zero homology in every positive chain degree. Thus the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism and these data form a ProjectiveResolution of B. For j greater than a.natAbs, -j is less than the lower bound a, so T.X j is zero. All of this helper is proved in Lean using Mathlib; no additional hole is introduced.

lean.statement:
theorem strictPerfectClosedPushforward_stalkResolution
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (x : Z) (U : Y.Opens) (hx : i x ∈ U)
    (K : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (hK : Y.IsStrictlyPerfect U K)
    (e : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf))) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) :
    ∃ (P : ProjectiveResolution
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (i.stalkMap x).hom).obj
        (ModuleCat.of (Z.presheaf.stalk x) (Z.presheaf.stalk x)))) (n : ℕ),
      ∀ j : ℕ, n < j → IsZero (P.complex.X j)
